comment: The mutants of fir.emptiness (src/fort/fir/emptiness.ft) that make the pass prove a store
that it must not prove, against the oracle test of rule (a) (test/fort/owner/oracle_test.ft,
spec/ownership-design.md 3.6). Each row is a row of tools/mutations/emptiness.json with the
same anchor. A row is caught when the test fails: a false accept makes it exit 134, and a
changed count changes its stdout. The log of a round shows which. D17.11-memory-pointer
changes only a count, because the pass stays sound with it: a place through a pointer local
that is memory changes only by a store into the local, which kills each fact with its base, by
a store through a pointer or a call, which kill each fact reached through memory, or by a
store into its pointee, which kills as any store does.
Of the 61 rows of tools/mutations/emptiness.json, 29 are not here: 13 make the pass prove
less, such as D17.11-memory-fixed, D17.11-straight-others and D17.11-call-after-check-same; 4
change the work limit, which no function of the sets reaches; 9 change the report, the driver
or the build-mode pass; and 3
prove more and change no verdict of a run. D17.11-below and D17.11-key-return change no run:
after the gen, an element of the span fails its bounds check first, and only a store writes
_0, which kills each fact with its key. D17.11-held-fixed stays sound: the place of a held
address of fixed storage reads as a local that is memory. The table runs in the Linux VM with
the debug preset and the default runner. The md5 guard reads the product compiler, whose driver
imports fir.emptiness. The first rounds of a run can read stale (notes/testing.md 7), so the
first row is one that a full run caught.

stages.name: the oracle test of rule (a)
stages.command: python3 test/lang/run_tests.py --root test/fort --fort build/Linux/debug/fort --std-dir build/Linux/debug/std --timeout 1500 -j 2 owner/oracle_test

mutations.what: a store into a key local kills no fact with that key
a store kills no fact with its base
a store through a pointer kills no fact of another base
a store straight into a global kills no fact through a pointer
a store straight into a memory local keeps a fact through a pointer that holds its address
a call kills no fact
the first statement after a check applies no kill rule at the check

mutations.old: apply_kills(c, s, d, !is_same(c, d, c->facts[cast(fact, u64)]), stale, fresh, pr);
mutations.new: apply_kills(c, s, d, false && !is_same(c, d, c->facts[cast(fact, u64)]), stale, fresh, pr);
mutations.what: the first statement after a check applies only the kill of its call at the check

mutations.what: a statement with a `void` destination after a check applies no kill rule at the check
the gen of a move operand comes again after the kills of its statement
a copy of a pointer local ends no freshness

            && (o.value.kind == fir.const_kind.ck_zero || o.value.kind == fir.const_kind.ck_null);
mutations.what: an aggregate of any operands is the zero value
a temporary that is memory keeps the value of its one store
an address of a local makes it no memory
a place through a pointer local that is memory is tracked
two places that differ first at an index are separate
a path behind a second deref, such as p->next->g, is separate from p->g
a temporary keeps the key of its source after a store into the source
a held address that is memory stays a held address
a held address reads as its place after a store into a local that the place reads
a stale held address gives a tracked place
a store through a stale held address keeps the facts through a fresh pointer
a call or a store into memory makes no held address stale
a call makes no held address stale
a store through a pointer or into a global makes no held address stale
a store straight into a memory local makes no held address stale
a move through a stale held address makes the place that it names now empty
the stale set joins by intersection
